title: Freddie Faber breaking his drumheads
summary: A drummer broke his drumheads, so Rudolph made him pay five dollars in advance.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Dance hall. There's a two or three dance hall down there. Now there's a fellow by the name of Freddie Faber. He's a drummer too. Or he's trying to be one of the two. But he broke my drum one night. And of course it didn't amount to much. But the next time I went down there I said, Listen Mr. Freddie, I said, I can't afford to be buying drum heads. I said, You take and let me hold a five dollar bill and you can go ahead and break them. I can buy some more. But I said, Me digging down my pocket, I said, That ain't no boy. Now they say he was a bad fellow. But I didn't mind talking man for my rights. And he gave him a five dollar bill and the first stroke he made, the stick went in the drum. He got up. But it was too late for him to get up. Then he hadn't broken. The first stroke he made. And the way he used to bang on them cymbals was the shit. And so I went home with these five dollars that night. I got two heads for that five dollar bill. Bottom and the top, it was all at the top of that rope. Next time I went down there, same old thing, give him a five dollar bill. He didn't break no that night, but I gave him his five dollar bill. When I went down there again, he said he didn't take no chance. I said, well that's one way of getting rid of him. He broke that when he paid for that one right after that. Yeah. Now, since then I haven't went. They beat up Papa Celeste. That was before he died.
